subject.title: Telegram: unquarantine skipped sticker e2e tests

question: Should OpenClaw require a dedicated Telegram static WEBP sticker metadata e2e case, or is the current resolver/cache/context coverage enough?
rationale: Current main partially satisfies the request and a closed unmerged PR later supplied proof, but protected maintainer/product-decision labels mean automation should not choose the Telegram coverage bar.

options.title: Adopt static WEBP e2e
options.body: Reopen or recreate the narrow 68845-style change, remove stale skip wording, and require Linux plus Windows CI proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept current coverage
options.body: Document that current resolver, cache-refresh, and context tests are sufficient for Telegram static stickers, then close this issue as a maintainer decision.

options.title: Defer until broader Telegram media sweep
options.body: Keep this issue open as owner-tracked test debt until the next Telegram media stabilization pass can batch proof across sticker and media paths.

recommendation.title: Adopt static WEBP e2e
recommendation.body: Reopen or recreate the narrow 68845-style change, remove stale skip wording, and require Linux plus Windows CI proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked stabilization commit created this exact follow-up and its unskip criteria.
